Q2153476.label: Social Christian Reformist Party
Q2153476.desc: Christian Democratic party in the Dominican Republic
Q2153476.summary: The Social Christian Reformist Party is a Christian democratic right-wing political party in the Dominican Republic. It was established on July 24, 1984, by the union of Joaquín Balaguer's Partido Reformista and the Partido Revolucionario Social Cristiano. Some of the PRSC's founders and leaders were originally business leaders and Roman Catholics who opposed the communist, socialist, and social democratic tendencies of Juan Bosch, the Dominican Revolutionary Party (PRD) and the Dominican Liberation Party (PLD).

Q17118212.label: Modern Centre Party
Q17118212.summary: The Modern Centre Party was a social-liberal political party in Slovenia led by Minister of Economical Development and Technology Zdravko Počivalšek, who succeeded former Prime Minister and former Minister of Foreign Affairs Miro Cerar as the party president. It formed in 2014 and merged with Economic Active Party in 2021, to form a party Concretely.

Q1581572.label: November–December 2009 Moldovan presidential election
Q1581572.summary: An indirect presidential election was held in Moldova on 10 November 2009 and 7 December 2009, following the parliamentary election held in July 2009.

Q1084932.label: 2008 Romanian parliamentary election
Q1084932.desc: elections for the Romanian Parliament, held on the 30th of November 2008
Q1084932.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Romania on 30 November 2008. The Democratic Liberal Party (PDL) won three more seats than PSD in the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate, although the alliance headed by the Social Democratic Party (PSD) won more votes and a fractionally higher vote share.

Q3177988.label: October 1959 Icelandic parliamentary election
Q3177988.summary: Early parliamentary elections were held in Iceland on 25 and 26 October 1959. Following the electoral reforms made after the June elections, the Independence Party won 16 of the 40 seats in the Lower House of the Althing.

Q600068.label: Centennial Olympic Park bombing
Q600068.desc: 1996 bombing in Atlanta, Georgia, United States
Q600068.summary: The Centennial Olympic Park bombing was a pipe bombing attack on Centennial Olympic Park in Atlanta, Georgia, United States, on July 27, 1996, during the Summer Olympics. The blast directly killed one person and injured 111 others; another person later died of a heart attack.

Q945668.label: 2007 Samjhauta Express bombings
Q945668.summary: The 2007 Samjhauta Express bombings was a terrorist attack that occurred around midnight on 18 February 2007 on the Samjhauta Express, a twice-weekly train service connecting Delhi, India, and Lahore, Pakistan.

Q1049092.label: October 2010 Sumatra earthquake and tsunami
Q1049092.summary: The 2010 Mentawai earthquake occurred with a moment magnitude of 7.8 on 25 October off the western coast of Sumatra at 21:42 local time. The earthquake occurred on the same subduction zone that produced the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake.

Q5318148.label: Dwight E. Evans
Q5318148.summary: Dwight E. Evans is an American politician and former educator serving as the U.S. representative for Pennsylvania's 3rd congressional district since 2016. A member of the Democratic Party, he previously served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, representing the 203rd district from 1981 to 2016.

Q1292804.label: Saint Lucia Labour Party
Q1292804.desc: social democratic political party in St Lucia
Q1292804.summary: The Saint Lucia Labour Party (SLP) is a social democratic political party in Saint Lucia. It currently holds 14 out of 17 seats in the House of Assembly.

Q1028.label: Morocco
Q1028.summary: Morocco, officially the Kingdom of Morocco, is a country in North Africa. It has coastlines on the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the Atlantic Ocean to the west, and has land borders with Algeria to the east; the Spanish exclaves of Ceuta, Melilla and Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera along the north, which it claims together with several small Spanish-controlled islands; and the disputed territory of Western Sahara to the south, partly occupied by Morocco since 1975. Morocco also claims to share a border with Mauritania through the disputed territory of Western Sahara.
